Different concentrations of sodium chloride solutions have different water potentials.
When onion cells are put into a sodium chloride solution with a lower water potential than the
cells, water leaves the vacuoles and the cells show plasmolysis.

• observe a sample of onion cells from S1, S2, S3 and S4

Carry out step 1 to step 7 to prepare a slide of onion tissue.
1. Label one dry and clean microscope slide, S1. Put the slide on a paper towel.
2. Put a few drops of sodium chloride solution, S1, onto the microscope slide.
3. Remove a piece of the onion tissue from S1. Peel off the inner epidermis as shown in Fig. 1.2.
The inner epidermis may start to separate or have become separated from the rest of the
onion tissue, so the epidermis may be floating in the sodium chloride solution.

4. Cut one piece of the epidermis so that it will fit under a coverslip. Put the remaining epidermis
into S1.
5. Put the piece of epidermis on the labelled microscope slide as shown in Fig. 1.3. If the piece
of epidermis is folded, you may need to add more drops of S1 so that it floats and can be
unfolded.

remove any excess solution that is outside the coverslip.

of light entering the microscope to observe the cells clearly.

In the investigation, three identical plants were put in flasks containing 70 cm of water as

The plants were each kept in different conditions:
• 20 °C + still air + high humidity
